newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Danger signs in race relations: Race relations in New Zealand had reached a precarious situation, concilator Rajen Prasad said on Wednesday. Page 1.

Alliance pledges invalid, says Kopu: Independent MP Alamein Kopu claimed on Wednesday night that she had been emotionally abused, bullied and threatened by Alliance leader Jim Anderton and deputy leader Sandra Lee, who had made it clear she was not wanted in caucus. Page 1.
Murderers 'most foul' face longer jail terms: Justice Minister Doug Graham is considering longer minimum sentences for what he on Wednesday said as "murder most foul". Page 1.

Kirton fires first salvo at government: Sacked associate health minister Neil Kirton has fired the opening shot in what is shaping up to be his lone battle against the one-seat majority coalition government from within. Page 2.

Suicide report gets mixed response: The government's discussion document on youth suicide was shallow and failed to tackle the lack of values among young people, the Christian Heritage Party said on Wednesday. Page 2.

Carter Holt head takes optimistic view of immediate prospects: Carter Holt Harvey's profits for the next three quarters will be better, on average, than the first quarter just ended, chief executive John Faraci said on Wednesday. Page 9.
CBD profit $340,000 in first five months: Property company CBD New Zealand has reported a tax-paid profit of $340,000 for the five months to June 30. Page 9.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Secret deal lets Irishman stay: MPs want answers on British role: Mysterious official sanction has allowed an Irishman imprisoned for possessing firearms in strife-torn Belfast to enjoy a haven in New Zealand.

Harsh words but no charges likely in winebox report: Former Serious Fraud Office chief Chas Sturt and former Inland Revenue Department head David Henry will today have their names cleared of accusations of criminal behaviour.
Peters furious about Kirton attack on PM: Winston Peters was on the war path on Wednesday following fresh attacks by his sacked minister, Neil Kirton, against the Prime Minister Jim Bolger.
ASB celebrates in style: ASB Bank has capped its 150th year in business by reporting a 29 percent leap in after-tax profit to a record $92.5 million for the year ended June.
TVNZ rates increase angers ad agencies: The advertising agency is protesting against an increase in TVNZ's rates for long-duration ads.
THE PRESS

Alliance bullied me -- Kopu: Abuse, bullying, and screaming matches within the Alliance caucus prompted list MP Alamein Kopu to desert the party that put her in Parliament, she said on Wednesday. Page 1.
MPs shocked by students' leaflet drop: Fears about Parliamentary security have been sparked after protesters have dumped hundreds of leaflets over MPs from the public gallery in the House. Page 3.

Rise in support for Shipley as leader: Transport Minister Jenny Shipley's fortunes are on the rise, with a new poll showing her support as preferred leader growing, amid continuing grumbles about Prime Minister Jim Bolger's stewardship. Page 3.
Tasman Ag lifted by one-offs: One-off gains have helped Tasman Agriculture to a higher bottom-line profit after a slight fall in operating earnings. Page 33.
ASB Bank eyes managed funds: Auckland-based ASB Bank is planning to expand in managed funds next month. Page 33.
